definitions: A yellowish or brownish bitter-tasting organic substance present in some galls, barks, and other plant tissues, used in leather production and ink manufacture.

Any of a group of astringent, bitter plant polyphenols that bind to and precipitate proteins and other organic compounds including amino acids and alkaloids. The term tannin is widely applied to a large range of polyphenolic compounds.
examples: The wine had a strong tannin.
Tannin is used in the tanning of leather.
